problem_statement: Predict hotel reservation cancellation (booking_status in {0,1}) from 17 booking attributes; synthetic Kaggle Playground tabular data (Season 3 Episode 7).

test_window.evidence: No true timestamp column; arrival_year/month/date cover the identical support in train and test (2017-2018, months 1-12, days 1-31) with matching year proportions (train 6050/36050 = 14.4% in 2017, test 4022/24046 = 14.3%). id is a contiguous non-overlapping index (train 0-42099, test 42100-70167), the standard Playground random row split, not a chronological cut. No forecasting wording in the description.

split_policy.scheme: StratifiedKFold (5 or 10 fold), shuffled, fixed seed; target rate 0.392 so stratification is a mild but free safeguard
split_policy.forbidden: GroupKFold or time-based split on arrival_* columns — there is no future test window and no group key, so a time split would only shrink the training set and bias CV
split_policy.notes: arrival_* is an ordinary feature here, not a split axis. Guard against the TASK-TS-FUTURE trap firing spuriously: the presence of date-like columns does NOT imply a temporal split when train/test share the same date support.

metric.name: ROC AUC
traps: rank-only metric: probability calibration is irrelevant, do not spend effort on Platt/isotonic
no threshold selection — submit continuous scores, never hard 0/1 labels
blending must be rank-safe: average ranks (or logits) rather than raw probabilities when members have different score scales
AUC differences on 28k test rows are noisy at the ~1e-3 level — do not chase CV deltas below that without repeated-seed confirmation

external_data.rationale: Competition rules in config.yaml set external_data_allowed: false and internet_access_allowed: false, so no external join is permitted regardless of usefulness. On the merits it would also be weak: the target is a per-booking behavioural outcome, all covariates that drive it (lead_time, price, market segment, request/cancellation history) are already present, and no country/currency/region key exists to join any whitelist source on. The only whitelist source with a derivable key would be a public holiday calendar via arrival_year/month/date, but the country of the property is not given, so the key is unresolvable.

data_level: reconstruct arrival date: combine arrival_year/arrival_month/arrival_date into a datetime; derive day-of-week, is_weekend_arrival, week-of-year, day-of-year, and a cyclical (sin/cos) month/day-of-year encoding

flag invalid calendar dates (e.g. Feb 29/30/31, Apr 31) produced by the synthetic generator — an is_valid_date indicator is often predictive in Playground data and is required before any datetime parsing
derive booking date = arrival date minus lead_time; adds a second seasonality axis (when the booking was made) independent of arrival seasonality
stay aggregates: total_nights = no_of_weekend_nights + no_of_week_nights; weekend_ratio; total_guests = no_of_adults + no_of_children; has_children

price normalizations: price_per_guest = avg_price_per_room / total_guests; total_revenue = avg_price_per_room * total_nights; price z-score within (room_type_reserved, arrival_month) and within market_segment_type — relative price is more informative than absolute
guest history: prev_total = no_of_previous_cancellations + no_of_previous_bookings_not_canceled; prev_cancel_ratio = no_of_previous_cancellations / max(prev_total, 1); interacted with repeated_guest
lead_time transforms: log1p(lead_time), lead_time bucketed, lead_time relative to the segment median — lead time is the classic dominant cancellation driver

CV-safe target encoding and pairwise crosses of the low-cardinality categoricals (market_segment_type x room_type_reserved, market_segment_type x type_of_meal_plan) — encoders fit inside the fold only

duplicate/near-duplicate row grouping across train+test on the feature vector: synthetic Playground data repeats rows; a group-size and group-mean-target (out-of-fold) feature is a cheap standard gain
model_level: GBDT trio as the backbone (LightGBM / XGBoost / CatBoost) with native categorical handling for type_of_meal_plan, room_type_reserved, market_segment_type — per TASK-CAT-ONLY evidence, native handling is where the accidental wins come from even when only part of the feature set is categorical
binary logloss / AUC-consistent objective; no class weighting or resampling needed at a 0.392 positive rate, and resampling would only distort the score scale
hyperparameter emphasis on regularization + moderate depth: 42k rows with 17 low-cardinality features overfits fast with deep trees

TASK-BLEND-DECOR: after the GBDT pool is built, add one shallow, heavily regularized, different-library member (regularized logistic regression on engineered features, or a small MLP) as a decorrelator before re-optimizing blend weights
blend on out-of-fold rank-transformed predictions and optimize AUC directly; hill-climb or NNLS-on-ranks, verified against a simple equal-weight rank average

considered_and_rejected_priors.reason: date-like columns are present but test shares the identical date support with train and the split is by contiguous id — not a future window; forcing a time split here would be the mirror-image of the s3e19 trap

no daily series with store/product keys and no country key for a holiday join, but calendar features derived from arrival_year/month/date are still legitimate row-level features (kept in injection_ideas.data_level)

only 3 of 17 features are genuine unordered categoricals (all cardinality <= 7); the rest are counts and continuous. Its action item (native GBDT categorical handling) is still carried into model_level
positive rate 0.392, far above the ~2% trigger
metric is ROC AUC, not an MAE-family metric
17 columns x 42k rows — rows greatly exceed columns
single scalar binary output, no generative grid/sequence structure

risks: date-column illusion: the strongest failure mode here is over-applying time-series machinery (time split, lag features) to what is an iid split — Stage 1 must confirm the iid verdict before any feature work
synthetic-data artifacts: Playground generators produce impossible calendar dates and repeated rows; treat both as signal-bearing flags rather than cleaning them away silently
AUC noise floor on 28k test rows makes public-LB chasing unreliable; trust repeated-seed CV
not_recorded: official competition rules text — only config.yaml special_rules was available offline (external_data_allowed: false, pretrained_models_allowed: false, internet_access_allowed: false); the live rules page was not fetched
public/private leaderboard split fraction of test.csv

whether the synthetic data was generated from an underlying real hotel-reservations dataset, and if so its identity — not determinable from the provided files, and moot since external data is disallowed
country/region of the property (blocks any holiday-calendar or macro join key)
